text: Provide a view of the complete control area with the actual outer switches, keycaps and centre control fitted together so their relative heights can be checked.
Keep model annotations limited to points that need attention. Clearly identify an unworkable design when presenting alternatives.

Update the guide with every permanent geometry revision. Show each latch and tab fitting, engaging and releasing with actual components and wiring. The whole-rod animation starts with the bare rod and runs continuously through assembly. Individual component views omit repeated rod-mounting steps.
The user guide should show where to click higher on the paddle, outside touch detection, for a precise click without moving the pointer.
For centre-control inspection, allow the four surrounding keys to be hidden together while the centre control remains visible.
The R58 bench build had the touch board, OP1 mouse switch and one outer key connected. This evidence covers the fitted controls only.

Provide the revision-specific model viewer link. Show the actual PCB, wired connector, retainers and their insertion order in an assembly guide for users. Animation must follow the real assembly path without jumping back and forth.
When a newer model is available, highlight the “Reload to see new version” button beside the assembly heading. Reload into that version and keep the selected component and view when available.
Provide a small drawing-mode button at the top left of the 3D viewer so the user can mark the displayed model and send screenshots to the agent.
